_why: Row 2903: `h_mad_failure_diff.py run` must end UNREADABLE reason=subject-changed when the subject tree changes during a subject run, including an edit reverted mid-run, and must not fire on ignored paths or its own --log-dir. Each mutant blinds one half of the snapshot comparison or widens what counts as the subject.
command: subject_tree_changed or ignored_path or log_dir_inside or log_dir_covering

mutations.name: S1: CHANGE IGNORED. A changed subject is measured as though it were the tree named in SUBJECT:, the pre-fix behaviour.
S2: SIZE ONLY. Comparing sizes alone misses an edit reverted mid-run, the reported case.
S3: TRACKED ONLY. A file created mid-run is not listed, so it is never seen.
S4: KEYS ONLY BEFORE. A path present after but not before is ignored, so a created file is missed.
mutations.find: return [rel for rel in sorted(set(before) | set(after))

mutations.name: S5: IGNORED PATHS COUNT. Listing ignored files makes __pycache__ writes read as a subject change.
S6: LOG DIR COUNTS. The run's own logs inside the subject read as a subject change.
S7: LOG DIR COVERS SUBJECT. A --log-dir equal to or above the subject excludes every file, so both snapshots are empty and a mid-run change ends SAME.
